title: Scanner page -- non-blocking pr-reviewer follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of frontend-market-scanner-page's PR #243, tracked here so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: Add a Playwright e2e spec under frontend/tests/e2e/ for the /scanner page (frontend-market-scanner-page): at minimum the golden path (category picker -> run scan -> results table -> add to watchlist) plus the disabled/unavailable state, matching the pattern of the existing dashboard/portfolio/watchlist specs. The persisted e2e suite currently has no coverage of the Scanner page at all -- only pr-reviewer's own one-off Playwright walkthrough exercised it.

Round 3 review nit: ScannerResultsTable.tsx's `ErrorOutlineIcon` is imported from `@mui/icons-material/ErrorOutlined`, not `ErrorOutline`/`ErrorOutlineOutlined`. `ErrorOutlined` is the 'Outlined theme' variant of MUI's `Error` icon (its SVG path is byte-identical to `Error.js`'s) -- a filled solid-circle error icon, not the lighter hollow-circle `ErrorOutline` family the variable name implies. Purely cosmetic (still clearly reads as an error) -- swap the import to `ErrorOutlineOutlined` (or rename the local alias to match `Error` if the solid icon was actually intended) so the name and the rendered icon agree.

Round 3 review nit: ScannerResultsTable.tsx's retry `IconButton` sets `disabled={addWatchlistItem.isPending}` inside the `if (addWatchlistItem.isError)` branch, but this is dead code -- TanStack Query's mutation reducer resets `error`/`isError` to `null`/`false` in the same synchronous dispatch that sets `isPending: true` (`@tanstack/query-core`'s `mutation.ts`, the `'pending'` case), so `isError` and `isPending` can never both be true and this branch is never actually rendered with `disabled` true. Harmless (clicking retry while a previous retry is still in flight just calls `mutate()` again, which TanStack Query already handles safely), but remove the dead prop or, if the intent was genuinely to disable the icon while a retry is in flight, use a separate local 'retrying' flag instead of relying on `isPending` inside the `isError` branch.

Round 4 review (non-blocking design note, distinct from that same round's blocking focus-loss-on-retry-success finding): ScannerAddToWatchlistButton's failure announcement uses `role="status"` (implicit `aria-live="polite"`) rather than `role="alert"` (implicit `aria-live="assertive"`). The round-4 fix's own `decisions` entry says this was chosen specifically so it wouldn't reintroduce the `queryByRole('alert')` landmark ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx's round-3 regression test asserts is gone -- but that test was written to confirm the *full ErrorState block* (an icon+heading+body element large enough to break row layout) was removed, not to forbid role="alert" on any element whatsoever; a visually-hidden live region with `role="alert"` would have zero layout impact and wouldn't reintroduce the layout regression the test actually guards against. WAI-ARIA authoring practice generally recommends `role="alert"` (assertive) specifically for action-failure announcements like this one, since a polite region can be skipped or queued behind other speech if AT is already announcing something else, whereas the alert role interrupts. Worth reconsidering as role="alert" (relaxing/rewriting the existing `queryByRole('alert')` test to target the ErrorState-block absence more precisely, e.g. asserting on a heading/testid rather than the alert role itself) the next time this component is touched.

Round 4 review (non-blocking, from a parallel code-review pass): common/UnavailableState.tsx's `message` prop is only rendered under a plain truthy check (`{message && (...)}`), so a backend `detail` of `''` (an empty string is a valid value for the `string | null` schema type, distinct from `null`) silently renders no message line at all -- both ScannerPage and ScannerPanel pass `message={data.detail ?? 'fallback text'}`, and since `''` is not `null`/`undefined` the `??` fallback never applies either, so the result is a bare heading with no explanation. Narrow (requires the backend/gateway to actually return an empty-but-present `detail` string, which isn't currently observed from any code path) but easy to close either by having `UnavailableState` treat a blank string the same as absent (e.g. `message?.trim() && (...)`) or by having the two callers coalesce an empty string to the fallback themselves (`data.detail || 'fallback text'` instead of `??`).
